scope: Portable runtime, harness installer, runtime build emission, native helper wrappers and tools/platform-native. Findings describe the reviewed pre-fix snapshot; other agents are applying corrections.

findings.claim: Uninstall removes preexisting skills because ownership is recorded for the whole collection from one directory check.
findings.evidence: Lines 103-106 check only .agents/skills/<packageId> and set a harness boolean. Line 71 removes every publicSkills entry whenever that boolean is true. A preexisting manifest-listed sibling skill is therefore removed when the packageId directory was initially absent; copied skill files also lack edit protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Track each installed skill file per actual harness destination, preserve preexisting files, and compare ownership hashes before removal. Test preexisting sibling skills and post-install user edits.

findings.claim: CLI-managed MCP servers edited or replaced after installation are deleted during uninstall.
findings.evidence: Claude/Codex removal is gated only by receipt.mcpAdded[name], while lines 117-118 save only true. No current-definition comparison precedes mcp remove. The OpenCode branch performs such a comparison, but the other two harnesses do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist the installed definition and compare it with current configuration before removal, or preserve CLI-managed entries with an explicit diagnostic when ownership cannot be established.

findings.claim: Claude installation silently ignores the requested revision while recording it in the receipt.
findings.evidence: --ref is accepted and saved in receipt.ref, but the Claude marketplace add branch passes only source and scope; existing marketplace update also receives no revision. The portableSource revision handling applies only to skills-based installations.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve and verify the requested revision before Claude installation or reject unsupported --ref combinations before any mutations.

findings.claim: Failed inventory probes are treated as proof that a plugin or marketplace is newly owned.
findings.evidence: probe permits nonzero status; marketplace and plugin branches ignore that status and treat unparseable output as absence. An idempotent successful add after an unsuccessful list can mark a preexisting resource owned, enabling its later removal.
findings.suggested_fix: Require successful, recognized inventory responses before ownership decisions; abort or preserve unknown ownership when inventory cannot be read.

findings.claim: The APK verifier certifies ARM64 using archive directory names without checking the ELF architecture.
findings.evidence: The only architecture condition is pieces[1] == arm64-v8a. The ELF tool receives only -d, which validates dynamic entries without rejecting a valid x86_64 ELF. Such libraries under the two required arm64-v8a filenames reach the ARM64 PASS output.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate each library's ELF class and machine as ELF64/AArch64; add a fixture containing valid non-ARM64 ELF bytes under arm64-v8a paths.

findings.claim: Portable installer subprocess failures lose their original exit codes.
findings.evidence: run throws a plain Error for nonzero child status and main always sets process.exitCode = 1. The native-helpers/common ToolError path preserves statuses, but installer operations using this runtime do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry child status in a typed error and preserve it in main; verify with a fixture command that exits 23.

checked_classes: Harness schema: current official Claude Code documentation explicitly supports command plus args as direct exec form; this is not a defect.
Converted native helper execution: inspected helpers use native process argument arrays; no direct Bash or Python invocation was found in the scoped helper sources.
Review is not Windows x64/ARM64 execution evidence, complete runtime certification, or cross-model verification.
